groups.label: The release workspace: what the robot runs

repos.desc: The workspace the team deploys. It holds no ROS packages of its own: each repo below is a git submodule in src/, pinned to an exact commit. Commit it before a pool test, tag it after; that pins what was in the water.
repos.extra: Also: scripts/ (Jetson setup, cross-building, Zenoh and DDS configs, service files) and zed_wrapper.repos, which pins the ZED wrapper and the image-transport packages for vcs import.
repos.name: riptide_release

repos.desc: The packages every other repo leans on: the custom messages, the vehicle description, and the hardware layer (sensor drivers, the EKF launch, the camera launch).
repos.name: riptide_core

packages.desc: The hardware layer. hardware.launch.py starts the CAN micro-ROS agent, DVL, IMU, gyro, AprilTag and acoustics; navigation.launch.py the robot_localization EKF (cfg/talos_ekf.yaml) and robot_state_publisher; zed.launch.py both ZED X Minis. Plus small Python nodes (actuator interface, depth converter, monitors).
packages.note: The monitor nodes in diagnostics.launch.py are out of date and not used, though talos_launch_mpc.yaml still starts them.

packages.desc: Custom messages, services and actions (riptide_msgs2): thruster commands and telemetry, firmware and kill-switch status, controller commands, mapping targets, the ExecuteTree action, and more.

The vehicle description: config/talos.yaml (mass, COM, inertia, thruster poses, sensor and camera frames) and the xacro that turns it into the URDF and TF tree. riptide_mpc reads it too. Nereus defines its own Talos (content/packs/robots/talos) and, for sim runs, writes a copy of this file with its plant's mass, COM and thruster poses (integrations/uwrt/launch/mpc_sim_model.py), so editing it doesn't change the simulated vehicle.
The team's VectorNav IMU driver, built on VectorNav's own C++ library (vnproglib 1.2, vendored in the package and left out of the line count). Publishes /talos/vectornav/imu.
Serial driver for the fiber-optic gyro (FOG): reads raw counts at 921600 baud and publishes /talos/gyro/raw, with health checks on temperature, supply voltage and light-source current.
A small node that compares pinger signal amplitude between two sampling windows ("was it louder before or now?"), from the amplitude stream the IVC board publishes.

repos.desc: Everything that turns "go there" into eight thruster forces: the MPC controller, the controller overseer and the thruster test tools.
repos.name: riptide_control

packages.desc: The controller Talos flies with: a model predictive controller on a Fossen model of Talos, with motion profiles, path following, a state estimator and pool system identification (pool_identify, identify_fit).

control_system.launch.py, which starts the controller overseer and then the active controller (active_control_model:=mpc picks riptide_mpc). Also the thruster test, calibration and tuning scripts, and the Simulink models of the older complete_controller.
packages.note: The Simulink complete_controller (sliding mode / PID hybrid) is the older controller; MPC replaced it.

packages.desc: A web page served from the robot (port 8090) to enable, kill and drive Talos from a phone. It drives on kill-switch slot 3 with needs_update, so the firmware kills shortly after the phone goes quiet.
packages.note: New: not committed, pinned or in any launch list yet. It exists only in a local checkout of the mpc branch, so nothing confirms it has run on Talos.

packages.desc: Keyboard and joystick teleop from the older stack. A COLCON_IGNORE file keeps it out of the build.

repos.desc: The detector and the course map. The Perception part of this site explains both in detail.
repos.name: riptide_perception

packages.desc: yolo_orientation.py: runs the YOLO segmentation model on each ZED image, then uses depth to turn masks into 3D poses. Separate models for the forward (ffc) and downward (dfc) cameras live in weights/.

mapping.py and map_estimator.py: fuse detections into one estimate per prop, with the course layout as a prior, and publish each as a TF frame the mission tree drives to. Also the binary classifier and the oriented/dependent frame publishers.

repos.desc: The mission code: BehaviorTree.cpp action/condition nodes in C++, the tree XML files in trees/, and the doTask action server (/talos/autonomy/run_tree) that runs a tree.
repos.name: riptide_autonomy

packages.desc: One package (riptide_autonomy2). include/riptide_autonomy/ holds the custom nodes in bt_actions/, bt_conditions/ and bt_decorators/ (FollowPath, SetMappingTarget, WaitForDetection, ...; some are implemented in src/riptide_autonomy/bt_actions/), trees/ the missions (RepairCompMpcTree.xml and friends), src/ doTask and the checkBT validator.

repos.desc: How the stack is started on the robot: the remote launcher service and the launch lists it loads.
repos.name: riptide_launch

packages.desc: The launcher that runs on the Orin as ros_launcher.service: starts the Zenoh router, serves a web page with a terminal, and starts or stops the launch files listed in launches/*.yaml (talos_launch_mpc.yaml is the full MPC stack; *_bench_* and *_sim_hil_* for the bench and HIL).
bringup.launch.py, a single launch file that includes hardware, navigation, control, detector, mapping and autonomy. On the robot the remote launcher's lists are used instead.
Messages, services and actions the remote launcher uses (start a launch, list PIDs, start a bag).

repos.desc: Driver for the Nortek DVL1000 (Doppler velocity log) over TCP. The pinned commit publishes velocity, status and a bottom-lock flag (dvl/bottom_lock). The newest commit on DvlWaterTrackFallback, not pinned yet, adds water-track velocity on its own topic, for when bottom lock is lost.
repos.name: nortek_dvl

packages.desc: The TCP driver node; publishes velocity and status. Its DVLConfig.txt is stale; the DVL's own web settings are the reference.
DVL message types (DvlStatus and friends).

repos.desc: A static transform that can be re-set at run time, or told to watch two frames and copy the average. Mapping uses it for the world to map transform; the model_tf action aligns map to the AprilTag-estimated origin.
repos.name: chameleon_tf

packages.desc: The node (mobile_tf.cpp).
Its ModelFrame action and services.

repos.desc: The open-source AprilTag detector (christianrauch/apriltag_ros), forked to add a SetBool service that turns its camera subscription on and off. The newest commit on CompressedImages, not pinned yet, lets it read the ZED's compressed image. riptide_hardware's apriltag.launch.py runs it on the forward camera. Its messages come from the apriltag_msgs submodule.
repos.name: apriltag_ros

packages.desc: The AprilTagNode component.

repos.desc: Upstream message definitions for apriltag_ros, pinned at version 2.0.1.
repos.name: apriltag_msgs

repos.desc: Stereolabs' ROS 2 driver for ZED cameras. Not a submodule: zed_wrapper.repos in the release repo pins it (and ffmpeg_image_transport, image_transport_plugins and friends) for vcs import. riptide_hardware's zed.launch.py starts two ZedCamera components, ffc and dfc. It needs the ZED SDK and an NVIDIA GPU.
repos.name: zed-ros2-wrapper

repos.desc: Software for the operator box (opbox), the team's Raspberry Pi field box: an HMI app for alerts and notifications, a ROS client that forwards robot state to it, and a small serial library.
repos.name: opbox_software

packages.desc: The opbox HMI application and its libraries (yaml-cpp vendored, not counted).
ROS 2 client that watches diagnostics and sends notifications to the opbox.
Keeps mapped values in sync over a serial link with custom frames. A nested submodule (BTK203/serial_library).

repos.desc: The simulator (nereus-sim) and the operator GUI (nereus-viewer), used for both the sim and the real robot. A submodule of the release repo since 2026-10-27, but built with its own CMake (COLCON_IGNORE), not colcon. All robot, pool and course data is YAML in content/packs/.
repos.name: nereus

packages.desc: 6-DOF marine dynamics of Talos with delayed thrusters.
Simulated IMU, gyro, DVL and depth sensors.
A run: tasks, props, mechanisms (claw, launcher, dropper, magnet) and scoring.
The OpenGL renderer for the 3D scene and the simulated cameras.
Stereo camera models with depth and point clouds.
Headless rendering of labelled synthetic images for training the detector.
Builds the 3D scene (pool, task props, robot) from a resolved scenario; shared by the viewer and the simulated cameras.
Schedules and queues captures from the robot's simulated stereo cameras during a run, without ROS.
Rigid poses and the fixed tree of named frames (sensor mounts).
The ROS 2 bridge for the simulator, and nereus-viewer itself with its panels (motion, autonomy, mapping, actuators).
The UWRT launch files (sim.launch.py, robot.launch.py) and acceptance scripts.
Pack tools (validate and resolve packs) and dataset tools.
The packs (robot, pools, RoboSub 2026 tasks, the Talos ROS bridge, datasets) and the viewer layout.
Competition scoring rules in C++.
Everything else in the repo: tests/, tools/ (checks, generators, benchmarks), the CMake build and docs.

repos.desc: C firmware for the RP2040 microcontrollers on every board, on the Pico SDK. micro-ROS over CAN makes each board a ROS node; titan_safety runs the kill-switch logic and fault reporting; a bootloader lets the boards be re-flashed over CAN without opening the hull.
repos.name: titan_firmware

packages.desc: Thruster ESC control (DShot) and telemetry; two of these boards drive the eight thrusters.
The power + actuator (POAC) board; it only arms the actuators while the robot is enabled.
Firmware for the Mark 2 power board (one of the boards riptide_hardware's board table lists).
Camera cage breakout board; reads the depth sensor.
Smart battery housings (BQ40Z80 gas gauge).
Inter-vehicle communication (acoustic) board.
Status LED board.
Firmware for the Mark 2 actuator board (project actuator_mk2), last changed in 2024-11.
Shared libraries (titan_safety, titan_bootloader, micro_ros_pico, CAN, depth and LED drivers). The Pico SDK is a submodule, not counted.
Host tools: canmore_cli for debugging boards over CAN, upload_tool for flashing, and DeviceList.jsonc, every board's serial number.
Board projects for Puddles, Lil Boat, Mercury (Triton) and the SBC board.

repos.desc: CANmore, the team's CAN bus protocol (128-byte packets over CAN frames). A C library for firmware and a C++ library for Linux hosts; titan_firmware and the micro-ROS agent both include it.
repos.name: titan_canmore

repos.desc: Builds the micro-ROS agent that bridges the boards into ROS 2: the agent (osu-uwrt/micro-ROS-Agent-impl), the team's Micro-XRCE-DDS-Agent fork with CAN support, and titan_canmore. On Talos it runs as micro_ros_agent can -D can0 (riptide_hardware's copro_agent.launch.py). At the pin that file also starts an "external network" agent on can1; the newest riptide_core commit, not pinned yet, comments it out.
repos.name: micro-ros-agent

repos.desc: In development: a lightweight replacement for micro-ROS. A Rust codegen reads a ros.toml listing a board's topics; a C library runs on the board; a host agent bridges to ROS. titan_firmware has a nano_ros branch; master still uses micro-ROS.
repos.name: nano_ros

repos.desc: The electrical team's Altium Designer workspace: board projects (schematics and PCB layouts) for Talos and older vehicles, the shared part library, design rules for JLCPCB 4-layer boards and a project template. Not code; the explorer counts design files instead of lines.
repos.name: electric_boogaloo

repos.desc: Sets up a new machine: installs ROS 2 Humble, clones the development workspaces with vcs import (riptide.repos), optionally clones the release repo, and adds the bashrc sourcing. Also colcon_riptide, the colcon plugin behind colcon deploy (sync sources to the robot and build there) and colcon timesync.
repos.name: riptide_setup

repos.desc: The second development workspace riptide_setup creates. Its repos are mostly also in the release repo now: nortek_dvl and chameleon_tf as submodules, zed-ros2-wrapper through zed_wrapper.repos. The other two are not used by Talos's launch files.
repos.name: development/dependencies

packages.desc: An older open-source VectorNav driver. riptide_hardware's own imu.launch.py still refers to it, but hardware.launch.py starts riptide_imu instead.
The upstream micro-ROS build tool (galactic branch), cloned by riptide_setup.

repos.desc: Builds ROS 2 C++ packages from the team's Simulink models with MATLAB R2023a (x86 and arm64), stages them in the workspaces (src/simulink_models/) and shares builds as GitHub releases, so you don't need MATLAB to run them. Used for the older complete_controller. Generated packages are not committed to any repo, so the release repo doesn't pin them. The riptide_navigation package that talos_launch_mpc.yaml starts ("simulink nav") looks like one of them, but its source isn't in any team repo we could find (unconfirmed).
repos.name: riptide_simulink

repos.desc: BehaviorTree Studio, the team's visual editor for BehaviorTree.cpp v4 XML (Electron + React). Works on a folder of tree files with a shared subtree library.
repos.name: btstudio

repos.desc: The team's fork of Groot, the older BehaviorTree editor. riptide_autonomy still keeps a Groot workspace (trees/.groot/workspace.xml) declaring every custom node.
repos.name: Groot

repos.desc: New: the pre-pool-test checker (command pretest), a Python/rclpy CLI that runs on the operator laptop and checks the repos, the bench and the robot before a test. Not on GitHub yet.
repos.name: pretest_checks

repos.desc: ROS 2 tutorials for new members on turtlesim (nodes, topics, parameters, services), in Python and C++.
repos.name: riptide_onboarding

repos.desc: Software for op-top, the team's operator laptop (an HP Omen); one node that drives its LEDs from riptide_msgs2 LedCommand messages.
repos.name: optop_software

repos.desc: The team's fork of the ffmpeg image transport (H.264/HEVC video over ROS). zed_wrapper.repos pins the upstream ros-misc-utilities version; riptide_hardware/cfg/zed_compression.yaml sets it to hevc_nvenc.
repos.name: ffmpeg_image_transport

repos.desc: Arduino code for the centre-of-mass scale: three load cells, weigh the robot nose-down then nose-up, and it prints the COM in the riptide_descriptions frame, ready to paste into config/talos.yaml.
repos.name: com_scale

repos.desc: ROS 2 packages and a GUI for measuring T200 thrust against command in a tank with a custom force gauge.
repos.name: thruster_calibration_tools

repos.desc: The fiber-optic gyro calibration rig: a heated enclosure on a stepper turntable, its Arduino sketch, a ROS driver and GUI, and MATLAB scripts.
repos.name: gyro_cal_rig

repos.desc: The previous simulator, replaced by Nereus. Still a submodule of the release repo.
repos.name: riptide_simulator

packages.desc: Fossen six-DOF plant, actuator model, simulated sensors and task scoring.
OpenGL pool viewer and simulated ZED cameras (DEPLOY_IGNORE, never sent to the robot).

repos.desc: The RViz-based operator GUI. The team no longer uses RViz; the Nereus viewer replaced it, for the sim and the robot. Still a submodule of the release repo.
repos.name: riptide_gui

packages.desc: RViz plugins for the old operator interface (control panel, mission panel). DEPLOY_IGNORE.
Meshes of the props and vehicles for RViz. DEPLOY_IGNORE.

repos.desc: An older physical kill switch with a stack light, run on a Raspberry Pi (robostop). Archived.
repos.name: riptide_kill_switch

repos.desc: An archived idea for a VS Code BehaviorTree editor; the repo holds only a README.
repos.name: behaviortree_vscode_extension

repos.desc: Not Talos. Mercury is a rewrite of the Riptide stack for Triton, the team's smaller second AUV (new for RoboSub 2026). mercury_release pins its repos as submodules the same way riptide_release does. Don't mix the two stacks up when searching GitHub.
repos.name: mercury_*
